description: Personalized nutrition mobile app with AI-powered meal planning, tracking, and recipe chatbot. Full-stack: Flutter mobile + Django REST backend + Firebase Auth + GPT-4o.
intended_use: Feed this entire JSON document to an AI coding agent (Antigravity, Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) as the single source of truth for building the project. The agent should reference this document for every implementation decision.

primary_developer_constraints.experience: Developer is comfortable with Flutter but new to Django.
preferences_stated: Wants Django specifically for ORM ergonomics
Wants production-grade Flutter (Riverpod, MVVM, reusable widgets, single ApiClient, exception handlers, deep linking)
Wants rule-based recommendation engine first, AI layered on top
Wants module-by-module build with clean, precise prompts to coding agent

project_agenda.summary: NutriPlan personalizes daily meal plans (breakfast/lunch/dinner) based on a user's biometrics, dietary pattern, allergies, and cuisine preferences. It tracks adherence, auto-aggregates calorie and micronutrient intake, and provides an AI chatbot that turns 'what's in my fridge' into actual recipes with validated macros.
project_agenda.core_thesis: Generic calorie counters are dumb logs. Recipe apps don't know your goals. NutriPlan combines a personalized daily plan + adherence tracking + AI improvisation into one loop.
primary_user_goals: Tell the app about me once → get a meal plan tailored to my body, goals, and food preferences.
See today's meals with full recipes, then check off what I actually ate.
Track calories and macros automatically as I check things off.
When I have random ingredients in my kitchen, ask the AI what to cook.
v1_locked_features: Meal tracker with status: planned / ate / skipped / substituted
Auto nutrition logging and daily/weekly aggregation
AI chatbot: free chat mode + ingredient-to-recipe mode

backend.ai: openai Python SDK v1.x (GPT-4o via Chat Completions with structured outputs)
backend.nutrition_reference: USDA FoodData Central API (free, requires api key)
backend.wsgi_asgi: gunicorn + uvicorn workers (ASGI required for streaming chat)

external_services.firebase_auth: Identity provider; issues ID tokens to Flutter; backend verifies via firebase-admin
external_services.usda_fooddata_central: Authoritative macro reference; validates GPT-returned recipe macros

tech_stack.hosting_recommendation_v1: Railway / Render / Fly.io for backend; move to AWS ECS or similar at scale
tech_stack.ci_cd: GitHub Actions (lint, test, build APK, deploy backend)

system_architecture.description: Flutter app → HTTPS with Firebase ID token → Django REST API → Postgres + Redis. Backend verifies Firebase token via firebase-admin SDK. Celery workers handle daily meal plan generation, nutrition aggregation, and OpenAI calls. OpenAI and USDA are called from backend, never from client.
data_flow: User signs in via Firebase Auth in Flutter → gets ID token.
Flutter ApiClient attaches Bearer token to every request.
Django FirebaseAuthentication class verifies token → loads/creates User.
Recommendation engine reads DietaryProfile + Recipe DB → produces MealPlan.
User logs meals → MealLog rows + DailyNutritionSummary updates.
Chat endpoint streams GPT-4o responses; macros validated against USDA before returning.

recommendation_engine.philosophy: Rules-as-policy, AI-as-creativity. Hard constraints (allergens, diet pattern, calorie window, prep time) enforced deterministically. Soft preferences (cuisine, variety, macro fit) scored numerically. GPT is a fallback for rare profile-constraint combos, never the primary engine.

steps: 1. HARD FILTER: meal_type matches, is_active=True, prep_time <= profile.max_prep_time_min.
2. DIET PATTERN HIERARCHY: vegan ⊂ vegetarian ⊂ pescatarian; omnivore = no restriction; keto and mediterranean strict.
3. ALLERGEN EXCLUSION: exclude recipes whose allergen_tags overlap profile.allergies (hard).
4. DISLIKES: exclude recipes whose ingredients match dislike text (case-insensitive regex).
5. CALORIE WINDOW: keep recipes within 75%-125% of slot_target (slot ratios: breakfast 0.25, lunch 0.40, dinner 0.35 of target_calories).
6. EXCLUSION: drop excluded recipe ids (used in regenerate).
7. VARIETY LOOKUP: find recipe ids used in this slot in last 7 days for this user.
8. SCORE each candidate: +30 cuisine match, +20*macro_match_score, -50 if in last_7_days, +seasonal_bonus (stub 0 in v1), + random tiebreaker 0..5.
9. Pick max-score candidate. Cap pool to 200 candidates for performance.
10. If pool empty after hard filters → raise NoSuitableRecipeError (M7 fallback hooks here).

when_used: Reasoning fallback: rule pool returns < 3 candidates → GPT generates custom recipe respecting constraints, persists as Recipe(source='gpt').
Substitution chatbot: 'swap chicken with paneer in today's lunch' → GPT rewrites, USDA validates macros.
Ingredient → recipe: structured-output JSON schema, USDA validation before return.
ai_layer.critical_rule: Never trust GPT macros. Always re-derive from ingredients × USDA before storing or showing.

properties.name: string
properties.instructions: array of string (one step per item)

nutrition_math.bmr_formula: Mifflin-St Jeor: 10*weight_kg + 6.25*height_cm - 5*age; +5 if male, -161 if female, -78 if other.

backend_build_specification.intended_executor: AI coding agent (Antigravity / Cursor / Claude Code)
backend_build_specification.build_mode: Module-by-module, sequential. Do not skip ahead. Each module must pass acceptance before next starts.
operating_rules: One module at a time. Complete fully (code + tests + migrations + acceptance) before next.
No speculative features. Only build what spec says.
Ask before deviating. Surface ambiguity; do not silently substitute.
Pin every dependency to an exact version in requirements/base.txt.
Tests not optional. ≥80% coverage on services. Every endpoint has at least one test.
Service layer enforced. Views thin (parse → service → serialize). Business logic in apps/<app>/services/.
Never trust client-supplied user identity. request.user is sole truth.
Idempotency: POST /tracker/log, /profiles/onboarding, /auth/register upsert on natural keys.
Structured JSON logs in prod. Service functions log entry/exit at DEBUG (no PII), errors at ERROR with stacktrace.
Every model change ships with migration in same commit.
Code style: black (line 100), ruff (E,F,I,B,UP,N), mypy --strict on apps/ and core/.
Commits: one per module. Format: feat(<module>): <summary> or test(<module>): ...
Do not use SQLite, even in tests. Tests run against Postgres.
Do not use Django default User. Use custom one from M1.
Do not write business logic in serializers or views.
Do not call OpenAI or USDA from model save() or signals. Always explicit service call.
Do not hand-roll JWT verification. Always firebase-admin.
Do not store API keys in models or settings literals.

endpoints.POST /api/v1/mealplans/regenerate: {date, slot} → updated plan; 422 NO_SUITABLE_RECIPE or 429 REGENERATE_LIMIT.

per_module_output_protocol: Before code: short plan (5-10 bullets, files to create/modify, key functions, test list) + open questions.

flutter_build_specification.architecture: Feature-first folder structure + MVVM via Riverpod. View = dumb widget; ViewModel = Notifier/AsyncNotifier; Repository = data abstraction; DataSource = wraps ApiClient.
per_feature_structure: providers.dart (all Riverpod providers for this feature)

api_client.implementation: Single Dio instance with BaseOptions(baseUrl=Env.apiBaseUrl, connectTimeout=15s, receiveTimeout=30s). Interceptors: AuthInterceptor, ErrorInterceptor, LogInterceptor in debug. Exposed as apiClientProvider.
api_client.auth_interceptor_behavior: On request: attach Firebase ID token (use cached unless expiring). On 401: force-refresh token, retry once.

exception_hierarchy.mapping: ErrorInterceptor maps DioException → AppException. ViewModels catch and translate to localized strings. ErrorState widget renders consistently.

routing.deep_linking: nutriplan://recipe/<slug> and https://nutriplan.app/recipe/<slug> configured in AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist.

production_essentials: Hive offline cache for today's plan (offline-first: show stale, revalidate)

local_environment: PostgreSQL 16 running locally (or via docker-compose) with empty DB named 'nutriplan' and user 'nutriplan'
Firebase project created at console.firebase.google.com with Auth enabled (email + Google)
Firebase Admin service account JSON downloaded → place at ./secrets/firebase-admin.json
developer_does_not_create: Database tables — Django migrations handle all schema
JWT verification logic — firebase-admin SDK handles it

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Rule-based engine first, AI as creativity layer (never primary)
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Deterministic, debuggable, testable, zero per-user cost, works offline, AI without rules drifts and hallucinates macros and ignores allergies.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Firebase Auth + Django (not django-allauth or SimpleJWT)
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: User stated preference; firebase-admin verifies tokens cleanly. Caveat: every backend write keys off firebase_uid not User.id for migration safety.
GPT is creative but unreliable on macros. USDA is authoritative. GPT for creativity, USDA for truth.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Service layer enforced; views stay thin
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Business logic testable without HTTP; easy to refactor; aligns with Django best practice for non-trivial apps.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Custom User keyed by firebase_uid as USERNAME_FIELD
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Backend never has password; Firebase owns credentials. Auth flow is verify-token → get-or-create-User.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: ASGI (uvicorn) for entire app instead of splitting sync/async
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: M7 streaming requires it; splitting now is premature optimization. Revisit if sync-endpoint latency becomes an issue.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Curated seed JSON instead of importing public dataset
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Faster v1 ship; quality control. Switch to public dataset import (RecipeNLG/Food.com) if scale demands.
